title: Per-Unit Cost Transparency Panel — prototype and pricing UI patterns
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a dedicated Console panel that surfaces per-unit (per-token / per-embedding) cost transparency for customers. The panel should support breakdowns by route/model, attribution to requests/sessions, downloadable export CSV templates, and UI patterns for presenting pricing tiers and estimated monthly spend. Aim for a single responsive panel that can be embedded in the existing Usage & Billing area and also surfaced as an endpoint in the Cost Insights dashboard.
context: Customers frequently ask why their hosted token costs spike and need an easy way to trace costs to specific routes and prompt patterns. Current console only exposes aggregate spend and token counts. This work pairs with runtime telemetry and billing tagging projects (ENG-50123, ENG-50988) to map telemetry -> cost at a per-request level. We need a design that: 1) scales to millions of requests, 2) surfaces sampled examples for high-cost buckets, 3) offers export-ready rows for accounting, and 4) shows pricing impact of batching/quantization recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: Panel mock exists in Figma with desktop and tablet states and clear system-level spacing tokens
Breakdown UI that can show: total cost, cost by model, cost by route, cost by prompt slice (label), and per-request sample with tokens/price
CSV/JSON export template documented with column list and sample row
Prototype includes pricing UI pattern to show effective unit price, tiered discounts, and an inline estimator (monthly projection)
Design passes accessibility check (color contrast, keyboard nav, screen-reader labels) and receives sign-off from PM and Eng
design_notes: Primary visual pattern: left column summary + sparkline + top contributing routes; center: searchable, paginated table with column-level attribution; right rail: open sample inspector and pricing estimator
Use a compact table row density by default; allow 'expand row' to show prompt/response snippet and tokens breakdown
Sampling policy: UI must clearly indicate that per-request list is sampled and link to telemetry sampling docs
Pricing UI pattern: show three states — list price, committed discount (if present), effective per-token price with tooltip detailing calculation
Export: default CSV includes ISO timestamps, route, model, prompt_label, tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_cost_usd, adjustment_key, billing_tag
reviews: 2026-03-05 — PM review (Ava Patel): Like the summary-first approach. Request: add a quick filter for 'most recent 7 days' and 'last billing cycle' presets.

2026-03-06 — Eng review (Sofia Rasmussen): Backend needs explicit contract for exported rows. Added dependency on ENG-50988 to provide per-request cost join keys. Also suggested adding a 'cost impact if batched' column with estimated delta computed by runtime heuristics.
2026-03-09 — Security (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed no PII in sampled prompt snippets; we must redact user-provided emails by default and surface a redaction toggle only for org-admins.
2026-03-12 — Design critique (internal): Adjust typography for table head to improve scan. Proposed microcopy for sampling disclosure and pricing tooltips drafted.
decisions: Keep per-request list sampled with explicit sampling rate in the UI; full raw export requires permission and an offline job to rehydrate (handled by ENG job: ENG-51300).
Pricing estimator will use a single effective_per_token field computed server-side. Frontend shows calculation tooltip and allows customers to toggle 'show committed discount' or 'list price'
Include a compact CSV template as default and an expanded CSV that includes raw telemetry ids and billing keys for customers with data access rights.

Sync with ENG (owners: Diego + Sofia) to formalize export schema and API endpoints — dependency ENG-50988 and ENG-51300
Write copy for sampling disclosure and pricing tooltip; handoff to content designer (owner: Priya Singh)
